bullet_feedback.bullet: Built an EventBridge-scheduled LLM-as-judge check for a production Amazon Bedrock classifier that rates research documents by importance to trigger fine-tuning only when its grades shift past a threshold
bullet_feedback.problem: Three stacked service/technique names ('EventBridge-scheduled LLM-as-judge check', 'production Amazon Bedrock classifier') come before the reader knows what the check does, and 'its grades' is ambiguous: it could refer to the judge or the classifier.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: A recruiter can't restate this to a hiring manager, so the one production-ML-ops bullet in the role gets skipped.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: whose grades shift (the classifier's vs. the judge's), and what problem this saves (e.g. needless retraining)
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Lead with the plain purpose (a scheduled check that decides when the document classifier needs retraining), then the method (a second model grading its output), and move 'EventBridge' to Skills or the end.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Designed the order book with std::list FIFOs per price level in a std::map and an order-ID hash map to make cancels O(1), which ran the full replay at 1.26M events/sec end-to-end
bullet_feedback.problem: The first two-thirds is C++ container names ('std::list FIFOs per price level in a std::map'); the only plain outcome is at the very end, and 'O(1)' is jargon to a non-engineer.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: The 1.26M events/sec figure is a headline number, but a skimmer has to wade through data-structure syntax to reach it, and a recruiter can't say what the design achieved.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Put the goal first (constant-time cancels / fast replay), then the structure in words ('a queue per price level plus a lookup by order ID'); keep 'std::map' only if it explains the choice.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Built the Claude skill’s main search tool by precomputing popular workflows from a 270K+ row PostgreSQL table into a Redis-cached category tree to keep lookups within the database’s permission and rate limits
bullet_feedback.problem: 'Redis-cached category tree' and 'within the database's permission and rate limits' are hard to picture; the bullet doesn't say what the search tool finds or for whom.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: The reader understands it's a search tool but not why limits were the problem, so the engineering decision doesn't land.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: what the 'permission and rate limits' were blocking (the AI skill querying the table directly?)
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Say the problem first (the AI skill couldn't query the 270K-row table directly because of access limits), then the fix (precomputed, cached category tree).

bullet_feedback.bullet: Rebuilt a legacy test-data workflow tool as a React and TypeScript Electron app with a visual React Flow editor and Jest-tested validation to make editing smoother, which 90% of 30+ surveyed developers preferred
bullet_feedback.problem: Five technology names in one clause ('React and TypeScript Electron app with a visual React Flow editor and Jest-tested validation') make it read like a stack list rather than a person describing what they built.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: It dilutes an otherwise strong, easy-to-repeat result (90% preferred) and pushes it to the very end of a full two-line bullet.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Cut 'React and TypeScript' or 'Jest-tested' to Skills; keep 'Electron app' and 'visual editor' since they explain what changed for users.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Built Redis caching in front of Tortuga’s Prisma ORM queries to reduce database load and latency for a class scheduler that drew 20,000+ visits in its first 30 days
bullet_feedback.problem: 'Tortuga' is never introduced; a reader has to guess it is the class scheduler. 'Prisma ORM queries' adds jargon without explaining the decision.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: The 20,000+ visits number is a clear user-traction signal but is attached to an unnamed product.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: that Tortuga is the class scheduler
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Name the product first ('Tortuga, a class scheduler that drew 20,000+ visits...'), then the caching; 'Prisma ORM' can move to Skills.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Built and prompt-tuned a pipeline for a PhD-led robotics project aimed at ICLR that overlays AnyGrasp’s candidate grasps on camera images in Open3D to help a vision-language model pick grasps that avoid hitting the table
bullet_feedback.problem: Long, single-sentence chain ('...aimed at ICLR that overlays AnyGrasp's candidate grasps ... in Open3D to help a vision-language model...'); AnyGrasp and Open3D are opaque tool names mid-sentence.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: The interesting idea (helping a robot pick grips that don't hit the table) is the last thing read; recruiters skip it, as I did on the skim.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Lead with the goal (helping a robot's vision-language model choose grips that avoid collisions), then the method; consider moving 'Open3D' to Skills.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Cut AI workflow generation time 65% to under 15s by splitting a Claude skill into focused sub-skills that call Python search and validation tools instead of relying on open-ended model search
bullet_feedback.problem: 'AI workflow generation' isn't tied back to the test-data tool in bullet one, so the reader isn't sure what is being generated or by whom.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: A small orientation gap; the 65% number is still memorable.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: that the workflows are the test-data workflows from the tool above
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Add a short anchor such as 'test-data workflow generation' so the three Capital One bullets read as one story.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Co-founded a 110+ member student product studio that has shipped 5 live products
bullet_feedback.problem: Pure scale statement with no engineering content; it uses one of three slots in the role.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: Minor; leadership signal is fine but doesn't support the 'systems engineer' story.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Fine to keep; optionally fold into the role header line to free attention for the engineering bullets.

page_feedback.problem: The intended 'systems-oriented engineer' identity rests mostly on the IEX order book project, which sits at the bottom of the page; the experience section reads as cloud + AI tooling.
page_feedback.why_it_matters: On a 7-second skim I took away 'AWS/AI builder', not 'performance-sensitive systems'; the strongest systems evidence is found last.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Consider whether the order book project's strongest bullet earns a higher position, or whether experience bullets can name the systems aspect (latency, capacity, caching) first.

page_feedback.problem: 'UMD App Development Contracting (Client: Amazon Leo)' is an unfamiliar org name next to a famous brand.
page_feedback.why_it_matters: A recruiter can't tell if this is a student club, a paid contract, or Amazon employment, and might wonder if 'Amazon' is being borrowed.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: clarify in the header what kind of organization this is (e.g. student-run contracting group) and keep the client in parentheses.

page_feedback.problem: Nearly every bullet fills two full lines and several stack 3-5 product names (React Flow, Jest, EventBridge, Bedrock, Open3D, Prisma).
page_feedback.why_it_matters: The page looks dense; the eye lands on bold numbers but the surrounding sentences are tiring to read, which lowers human voice and plain language.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Move tool names that don't explain a decision to Technical Skills; the Skills section already lists most of them.
